'''''Nicotiana sylvestris''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the nightshade family [[Solanaceae]], known by the common names '''woodland tobacco''', '''flowering tobacco''', and '''South American tobacco'''. It is a [[biennial plant|biennial]] or short-lived [[perennial plant]] in the [[tobacco]] genus ''[[Nicotiana]]'', [[native plant|native]] to the [[Andes]] region in Argentina and Bolivia, in South America.

==Description==
It is a tall plant, growing to {{convert|1.5 |m|ft|abbr=on}} high by {{convert|0.5 |m|ft|abbr=on}} broad. The [[leaves]] are simple, somewhat sticky, with the blade partially surrounding the stem, clasping [[petiole (botany)|petiole]].{{cn|date=June 2024}}

Flowers are produced on many-branched stems.<ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> The flowers are tubular, white, borne in [[raceme]]s held above the foliage.  Flowers can be over 7 cm long with a face 2 cm wide. Their intense scent is strongest at night, to attract pollinating moths. Each flower eventually produces a large quantity of small seeds. {{cn|date=June 2024}}

This plant is thought to be one of the parents of ''[[Nicotiana tabacum]]'', the plant used in modern [[tobacco]] production.<ref>Kawashima, N. 1976. Origin of ''Nicotiana tabacum'' detected by primary structure of fraction I protein. ''Biochim Biophys Acta'' 427(1):70-7.</ref> However, all parts of ''N. sylvestris'' can cause discomfort or irritation if consumed.{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}}

==Cultivation==
''Nicotiana sylvestris'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]] as it has fragrant and visually interesting flowers.<ref name="ley196512">{{Cite magazine

While most ''Nicotiana'' species and members of the ''[[Solanaceae]]'' family are naturally short-lived perennials, ''Nicotiana sylvestris'' is typically cultivated as a half-hardy annual in cold climates. Gardeners usually start seeds indoors under heated conditions in early spring, then transplant seedlings outdoors once frost danger has passed. In Great Britain, this plant can only survive winter outdoors in particularly sheltered coastal regions or select London neighborhoods where temperatures remain above −5 °C (23 °F).{{cn|date=June 2026}}

[[Cultivar|Cultivars]] of this plant have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name="RHS">{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Nicotiana sylvestris''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/69785/Nicotiana-sylvestris/Details | access-date = 16 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 69 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 13 April 2018}}</ref>
